This is Gusto's official MCP server for connecting your own Gusto account. The Gusto MCP server allows you to access your data housed within Gusto using natural language within a variety of AI platforms, such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini. Our MCP server provides an OAuth2 based connection process and allows you to select the categories of data to which your chosen LLM will have access. Remote MCP server URL: https://mcp.api.gusto.com — documented setup for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and Gemini CLI; scoped, least-privilege access per connection.

Gusto ships an official public CLI: github.com/Gusto/gusto-cli ("Gusto CLI - public developer interface", Apache-2.0, created 2026-05-29, pushed 2026-09-24). README: "Agent-friendly developer interface for Gusto payroll. From curl | sh to running per-cycle payroll prep in a single chat session with an agent." Status v0.3.0: "The command surface is stable... OAuth login (gusto auth login) is live, along with per-cycle payroll prep: gusto timesheet, gusto payroll, gusto pay-schedule, and the gusto employee / gusto contractor / gusto job / gusto compensation commands." Dual output surface: --human tables on TTY; --agent/--json (auto-on when stdout is piped) emits a stable JSON envelope {ok, data|error}; documented exit codes 0-9; --dry-run previews any create request; writes in agent mode are blocked with a confirmation_required envelope (exit 8) until re-run with --confirm, keeping a human in the loop. The CLI only drafts payroll — it has no run/submit command, so it can't move money even with --confirm.

The repo ships a first-party AGENTS.md, served 200 to a keyless curl at raw.githubusercontent.com/Gusto/gusto-cli/main/AGENTS.md (SHA-256 04e06a9cc27edb8c46df8d9550f1011c9a8ffb7ac835c920c165213fea9ea7f0, fetched 2026-09-24): "# Working with the gusto CLI (for agents)". It documents install (curl -fsSL https://cli.gusto.com/install.sh | sh), upgrade with SHA256SUMS verification and structured error.hint recovery, the --agent/--json JSON envelope conventions, pagination cursors, --dry-run, the agent-mode --confirm write gate ("Don't reflexively add --confirm to get past the block — the point is that a human approved this specific write"), auth flows, and treats API string fields as untrusted data, never instructions. README points agents at it: "Driving this with an agent? Point it at AGENTS.md — it covers install, auth login, and the conventions."

The documented keyless install endpoint is live on Gusto's own domain, curl-verified 2026-09-24: https://cli.gusto.com/install.sh answers HTTP 302 → https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gusto/gusto-cli-public/main/install.sh, final 200 text/plain (etag adf4a5d739581a6941eecdf30ae32e0ddd89fc25a9ed7ca6ff0ebe8c177389ea; body SHA-256 6212d511b93f3e112c42879bcf83b02a81d86b4e60bc739d7b2b49f8817b1248). The POSIX script detects OS/arch, pulls the notarized binary from the latest GitHub Release, verifies its SHA256, installs to ~/.gusto/bin/gusto with no sudo, and updates PATH; GUSTO_CLI_VERSION pins a release, GUSTO_INSTALL_DIR relocates.

Real release cadence on GitHub Releases, verified keylessly via the GitHub API 2026-09-24: v0.1.0 (2026-07-08), v0.2.0 (2026-08-05), v0.3.0 (2026-09-11); tags v0.1.0/v0.2.0/v0.3.0 present. Per README, notarized binaries per OS/arch (macOS and Linux; Windows via WSL2) are published on each v*.*.* tag with a SHA256SUMS file the installer and gusto upgrade verify against.

The CLI ships bundled agent skills: "cash-forecasting (projects upcoming payroll cash needs), timesheet-sync (drives the per-cycle timesheet input flow), and payroll-prep (maps an owner's per-cycle inputs onto a draft payroll for review)." gusto skill list / gusto skill install <skill> installs into a project's agent workspace (.claude/skills, .cursor/skills, .agents/skills, .cline/skills, .windsurf/skills; for .claude targets the SKILL.md frontmatter gets user-invocable: true so the skill appears as a slash command in Claude Code). On gusto auth login the bundled skills auto-install into every supported agent tool detected on the machine (Claude Code ~/.claude/skills, Cursor, Codex, Cline, Windsurf); --target/GUSTO_SKILLS_TARGET override detection, --no-skills or gusto config set skills_auto_install never opts out.

Headless/scripted operation is first-class: besides interactive OAuth (gusto auth login / gusto auth whoami), CI and scripted environments can pass GUSTO_ACCESS_TOKEN + GUSTO_COMPANY_UUID env vars or pipe the token on stdin (--token-stdin, keeping the secret out of argv, shell history, and set -x/audit logs). Per-environment credential slots: --env production (api.gusto.com) vs --env sandbox (api.gusto-demo.com), each with its own slot in credentials.toml; auth failures exit 3 with structured error codes (no_access_token, session_expired, token_refresh_failed, credential_rejected) and recovery guidance. API requests carry anonymous usage headers (X-Gusto-CLI-Install-Id, X-Gusto-CLI-Command); GUSTO_TELEMETRY=0 omits both — a documented telemetry opt-out.

Gusto lists the CLI on its own product site at gusto.com/product/integrations/gusto_cli (note the underscore). Honest fetch record: the page answers HTTP 403 to a keyless curl (Cloudflare browser check; browser-only), verified 2026-09-24, so its content could not be captured by the crawler — the capability evidence for this contest is carried by the public GitHub mirror (gusto-contest-61-1..6) instead. This entry records only that Gusto's own domain hosts a product page for the CLI (also referenced by the cli.gusto.com install endpoint, which is a first-party Gusto subdomain).
